packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-06 - unverified image reading (first reader)

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE NOTE
No proposed identification or earlier reading of this item was in my context. (I had read
packets 04 and 05 before this one, as instructed; they are different items.) I listed the
packet directory once for file names; packet.json was not opened. Nothing was rotated or
processed for this packet.

LAYOUT SURVEY
Images: image-001.jpg (reduced, with mm/cm scale) and image-002.jpg (native tile) show one
side, here "side A"; image-003.jpg (reduced, with scale) and image-004.jpg (native tile)
show the other side, "side B". Which is recto and which verso cannot be told.
Observations:
- A very small parchment fragment, about 3 cm wide and about 4.5 cm high by the scale, in
  two pieces (upper and lower) laid together along a straight horizontal cut; the lower
  piece is slightly narrower and sits a little askew. Upright.
- Script: a tiny, rapid, extremely abbreviated Latin Gothic cursive/"notula"-type hand,
  brown ink, about 10 lines in 4.5 cm. Many superscript letters and suspension strokes.
- Each side shows parts of TWO columns with a blank intercolumnar space about 1 cm wide:
    side A: line ENDS of a left-hand column (c. 8-12 letters per line) + intercolumn + the
            first one or two letters of the lines of a right-hand column at the right edge
            (paler, partly lost);
    side B: the last one or two letters of the lines of a left-hand column at the left
            edge + intercolumn + line BEGINNINGS of a right-hand column (c. 6-10 letters).
  So the fragment is a vertical strip cut through the gutter between two columns.
- A dark vertical stain/crease runs down through the written part on both sides (a fold,
  perhaps from use in a binding - tentative).
- No rubric, running title, enlarged initial, underlining or gloss on what survives. A
  tiny speck of red at the top edge (side B) and at the bottom edge (both sides) may be
  remains of red ink (paragraph mark?) or accidental - uncertain.
- Tentative interpretation of content: scholastic prose (abbreviations of the type used for
  "forma substantialis", "motu(s) locali(s)", "secundum", "sed", "non"); this is a reading
  of the abbreviations, not an identification.

Selected: everything; there are only about ten short line-fragments per side.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
SIDE A - image-002.jpg (native tile; image-001.jpg is the same view reduced)
The horizontal cut between the two pieces falls between lines 5 and 6.

Left-hand column, line ENDS (beginnings lost at the left edge):
 1: [...] [.]t(?) ab al[..]ac̄e(?) / ab alt(er)āte(?)   (word after "ab" begins "al", middle in the stain,
                                                      ends "-re"/"-te"/"-ne"; two small marks above)
 2: [...] ⁊ d(e?)[..]n[..]to / [..]m(od)o(?)             ("⁊" + "d" with superscript; end "...neto"/"...mo"; stained)
 3: [...] mo(tu?) a(?)i(?) locali                        (reads "moai locali" / "mo aī locali"; "locali" is clear)
 4: [...] [.]rādu(m?) s(ecundu)m(?) q(ui)a(?) [.]9       ("rādu"/"rādiū" with stroke; then an s-form with
                                                      stroke and superscript, a "q"-group; -us sign at end)
 5: [...] [..]uō c(?) uix(?) s(ed)                       ("uō"/"nō" with stroke; "uix"/"nix"; final "ſ3"-like sed/s; )
 6: [...] [.]uc(?) dic̄(?) s(ed) d(?)                     (first line of the lower piece; "...uc dr̄/dic̄ ſ; d" with
                                                      superscript letters above the end)
 7: [...] [.]u s(ecund)o(?) q(ui)a(?) c[..]o(?)          ("ſ" with superscript o; then "q"-group; last word with a
                                                      superscript "o" and a cross-like mark beneath)
 8: [...] [.]i(?) uir[..]te(?) o(mn)e(?)ꝯ / [..]e eoꝯ    (long stroke above the first word: "uīrt.."/"un̄ite";
                                                      line ends with the "ꝯ"(-us/con) sign)
 9: [...] foᵃ ſbal'                                      (= fo(rm)a s(u)b(stanti)al(is)? - "fo" with superscript a,
                                                      then "ſ", superscript b, "al" with a final stroke; clear letters)
10: [...] [..]lit(er?) mult[..]                          (bottom line cut by the lower edge; "…li…mult…" only)

Right-hand column, first letters of lines (paler, at the right edge; line positions matched
to the left column by height):
 1: g(?)/s(?)[...]        2: a(?)/o(?)[...]        3: m[...] (with stroke above: "m̄"/"in")
 4: ⁊(?)/7 [...]          5: o(?)[...]             6: [lost]
 7: [trace]               8: ō[.](?) / dī(?) [...] (letters with a stroke above)
 9: au(?)/cu(?) [...]    10: ō(?)/ē(?) [...]

----------------------------------------------------------------------
SIDE B - image-004.jpg (native tile; image-003.jpg is the same view reduced)
The horizontal cut falls between lines 5 and 6 of the right-hand column.

Left-hand column, last letters of lines (at the left edge), top to bottom as they appear:
  a: [...] m          (large "m", topmost, slightly above line 1)
  b: [...] ao(?) / ac(?) / as(?)
  c: [...] a
  d: [...] po(?) / ꝓ(?)   ("p" with superscript o, or pro-sign)
  e: [...] [.]y(?) / iꝫ(?)
  f: [...] o          (preceded by a point)
  --- cut ---
  g: [...] g(?) / ꝯ(?)   (a large hooked sign)
  h: [...] [traces of two lines, faint strokes only]
  i: [...] ꝺꝺ(?) / &c(?)  (a group with a long horizontal bar through it - possibly "ꝑt"/"ēē";
                           I cannot decide)
  j: [...] īe(?) / n̄e(?)  (two letters under a long overline: "ie"/"ic"/"te")
  k: [...] nō          (= non, clear, with overline)
  l: [...] o(?)        (with a dash before it; bottom edge)
(12 positions against 10 right-column lines: the left column seems to have slightly
closer line spacing, or two of these are superscripts; not resolved.)

Right-hand column, line BEGINNINGS (ends lost at the right edge and in the dark stain):
 1: ad e[.]liq(?)[...]      ("ad" clear; then "e"+"cl"/"d"; "-liq"/"-lig" with a tail; superscript above)
 2: ess[..]ſp(?)[...]       (begins "eſſ"/"aſſ"; long-s forms with a stroke above at the stain: "eſſe ſp̄"?)
 3: mexi(?) ⁊ a(?)[...]     ("m" + "e/a" + "x" + minim: "maxi"(=maxime?) / "mexi"; then a horizontal
                             stroke/⁊ and "a"/"ca")
 4: g(ener)ib(?)[..] ⁊(?)[...]  ("g" with a hooked superscript, then "ib"/"lib", stain, a 2-shaped sign)
 5: In ip̄o(?) 4[...]        ("In" then a group "iꝑi"/"ipō"/"iᵗᵒ", then a figure like "4" - possibly the
                             numeral 4 (quarto) - with a stroke after)
 6: q ꝛ(?) leuix(?) ī(?)[...]   (first line of lower piece: "q" + 2-shaped sign (q(uia)/q(uod)?), then
                             "l"+"eui"/"ēn"/"om" + "x"; then "ī" with stroke: "in"/"est")
 7: dc̄ao(?) / d(i)c(t)a o(?)[...]   ("d", "c" , "a", "o"-like letters with a looped superscript ("cs"/"o") above:
                             possibly d(e)c(lar)a(ti)o / d(i)c(t)a c(um)?)
 8: ecl(?)cū(?) / calciu(?)[...]    ("e/c"+"a/c"+"l"+"c"+minims with stroke: unresolved)
 9: ſi ille(?) nō(?)[...]    ("ſi" then "ll" with superscript "c"/"e" ("illᵉ"), then "n̄o"/"uō" with overline)
10: [.]a[.]oc̄e(?) / [..]tione(?)[...]   (bottom line, cut by the edge; long overline; red speck below)

----------------------------------------------------------------------
UNREAD / LIMITS OF THIS READING
- All of it was examined at native resolution; nothing was skipped. The readings are
  nevertheless weak: this hand resolves into words only with context, and each line gives
  at most two or three words. I have not completed words from sense.
- Most secure strings for a later match: side A line 3 "...locali"; side A line 9
  "foᵃ ſbal'" (forma substantialis, if the expansion is right); side B line 1 "ad ...";
  side B line 5 "In ... 4"; side B line 9 "ſi ill(e) nō"; side B left column "nō".
- Column order: on each side one cannot tell from the fragment alone whether the leaf had
  just two columns; I treat the visible pair as columns a/b of one page. The sides cannot
  be ordered (recto/verso unknown), so the reading order of the four column-fragments is
  open.
- The dark vertical stain hides one or two letters in nearly every line on both sides.

SUGGESTIONS
- A UV or infrared image of the stained band would probably recover the hidden letters.
- If other strips from the same binding exist, the adjacent strip to the left of side A
  (= to the right of side B) would complete these lines.

This is an unverified image reading.
